——

“Mydeimos!” a golden-gilded, floating mannequin hissed, shocking him out of his stupor.

He swallowed and felt the saliva go down thick, tracked it, as if that would ease the lock of his muscles. It didn’t.

Glancing down, thick, red liquid stained his fists and slid onto the pure, shining white tiles beneath his hunched figure. They were likely freshly cleaned; he could make out his reflection blinking back at him. A pity.

In front of him, the training grounds were in carnage. Where the tiles shied away from packed dust, wood was split in half, the sharp, jagged bits glinting menacingly towards the high sun– a splinter waiting to happen. The training dummies, now without their poles, were strewn about in a fashion only comparable to a battlefield, the hay stuffing torn out and now scattered in the noon wind. Dark streaks painted the ground itself– loose in some places, stomped into stone in others. The only presentable thing left– that survived– was the weapon’s rack, and that was still with several spears missing. If one peered close enough, they would find the remains of those scattered about, too.

Methodically, like easing a cramp, Mydei let the deformed pomegranate fall from his grip. “...Yes?”

A golden nymph was perched upon the mannequin’s shoulder. “I believe destruction of public property was amongst one of the Okheman rules we discussed upon your arrival.”

“Indeed,” he sighed and shook his hand, “but it’s no matter. I can assure I’ll have it cleaned by the recruits’ evening classes.”

“All by yourself, I presume?”

He nodded, a jerky motion. No matter how much he shook his hand, the pomegranate juice still clung to his skin, sticky and unbearably itchy. But not where he could reach, no, that would be far too easy. Instead, it spread just beneath the skin, up his arms, up his throat…

By his side, his clean fist twitched. The nymph seemed ready to leave him be, but then a small, hesitant sigh echoed from its body. “Mydeimos, are you alright?”

Another nod. “I apologize for my outburst; it won’t happen again.”

Silence followed. Painful, knowing silence that never failed to make Mydei want to bury his head beneath the dirt and never surface. But Aglaea, bless her, relented without another word, and the mannequin floated off to guard another, more relevant post. Left alone once more, Mydei sighed. His whole body seemed to slump with the force of it. With only his thoughts, that itch became only more difficult to ignore.

Usually, granted he gave it enough effort, every urge and petty craving eventually bowed in defeat and retreated back to the recesses of his mind. Thus far, Mydeimos was undefeatable, and he took the utmost pride in that. ‘30% Training, 70% Diet’ was his motto online, after all.

Mydei was not an angry man. Mydei was not a violent man. Titans forbid, Mydei was not an insane man.

But this feeling, this all-consuming urge, must have made the long crawl from his brain to down the curve of his spine and nestled in his weakest spot. It was outrageous, yet it locked his muscles in a constant battle stance, prickled at the most innocent of things, and Mydei, an unwilling hostage, snapped at the well-meaning. Even the ever-bright Deliverer hadn’t been spared.

The worst part about it? The root of it all escaped him.

So, Mydei was reduced to this– a glowering man left to pick up the pieces of his defeat. Slowly, he gathered up all the broken dummies and disposed of them properly, even setting up new ones for the recruits if only to distract himself. Dirt stuck to his juice-stained hand and it made him want to scream. 

In fact, he distracted himself so well that by the time the clock struck Parting Hour, the training grounds had been thoroughly cleaned and organized. Every weapon was in its place, the dirt was packed, tiles were polished to perfection, and Mydei… almost felt normal again. Almost. If he failed to think hard enough for long, he could tell it was there, lurking. It was only when a pot to his right fell with a crash that his peace was broken.

“My, my… I really like what you’ve done with the place,” a woman purred, her nails glinting from the shadows, shards of clay spread by her feet.

“Cipher,” he started, but then clamped his mouth shut. Mydei did not need Cipher of all people figuring out his current… issues. Instead, he kept it short. “What are you doing here?”

“What, a cat can’t miss her friends?”

She sidled up to him, her tail flicking against him like the nuisance she was. “Besides, you seem rather tense, little lion. More than usual. What gives?”

“It’s none of your business.”

“None of my business?” Cipher gasped– though she clearly regretted it as her nose wrinkled. “It’s my business when you’re gassing the entirety of Okhema with your sweat! You smell like fish, and not the delicious kind– odd, because that Deliverer boy always–”

She stopped herself. As the corners of her lips twitched up, Mydei felt an overwhelming sense of dread coat him like a shroud. Then, Cipher stepped back, looked him up and down with the scrutiny of a cat who got the cream. There was a sparkle in her eye when she finished, one that made Mydei feel everything but joyous.

“Oh… oh. That’s quite a mess you’ve gotten yourself into, hm? Well, don’t get your panties in a twist, I won’t pry!” Cipher waved her hands as if she were a generous boss discussing an employee’s sick days instead of… of…

But Mydei was too stunned to scowl. “Really?”

“Truly and honestly, little lion! Aglaea told me to behave, so who am I to disobey?”

Cipher pointedly ignored the unsure glance towards her and instead shrugged, her body practically humming with energy. “Though, at least let me give you a spritz of my perfume or something, because you’d be bold walking back to your chambers smelling like that.”

Mydei pursed his lips. On one hand, his instincts and common sense told him to refuse, to run far, far away from whatever this trickster had to offer as ‘help.’ On the other, however, a quick whiff told him that his impromptu workout amongst dirt and grime did him no favors. The Deliverer would show up soon, and despite the fact that Mydei had full intent on avoiding him, he still refused to be caught dead smelling like this. If he was, surely the bath invitations would be endless.

Slowly, like he was already regretting it, he nodded. Cipher wasted no time whipping out a full bottle of perfume and dashing around his stiff body. Pink, he absentmindedly registered, the perfume was a brilliant pink. His favorite color. It was ironic, the farthest from fitting Cipher at all, yet he sat still and let her have her fun. She spritzed around his armpits, his thighs, his neck, and lastly, one big poof of pink in his face. Mydei squeezed his eyes shut.

“There! Purr-fect, if I do say so myself!”

It was cloyingly sweet, overwhelmingly so. It filled his nostrils and clung to his senses– though didn’t choke him. Instead, it merely settled heavy in his lungs, akin to a weighted blanket on his troubled mind. How strange. If he thought about it hard enough, Mydei could pick up strong fruity notes and even the softer, more feminine floral undertones that made the scent blossom. Briefly, he recalled Cipher's signature scent: leather and spices.

His tongue felt like lead. “This… this isn’t your perfume.”

“Is it not?” She hummed, pocketing the bottle as soon as Mydei opened his eyes. “I thought I’d try something new, you know? A little sparkle to spice things up. It can be helpful, even to a shy grump like you!”

Cipher winked obnoxiously, and with a dramatic flourish, she vanished, only a kicked-up trail of dust in her wake. Mydei simply stared after her. He swallowed, shifted on his feet a little– didn’t quite know what to do with himself. That was common with Cipher, Phainon had once assured him, as she never got a better kick out of anything but leaving people confused. But this was different. His limbs were heavy, not twitching with barely constrained energy or need. His muscles were relaxed. And his mind… his mind was blissfully silent.

Light flickered amongst the pillars that guided recruits and nosy, white-haired swordsmen to the training grounds. Soon, voices followed, many of them. Right– evening recruitment training. A spark of panic lit in his chest and, with the grace of wading through a swamp, he stumbled through a less-used exit and disappeared into the quieting streets of Okhema.

His chambers were dark when he arrived; the blackout curtains were already sealed tightly shut. With a deep sigh, Mydei forewent the bath and instead flopped on his kline, the many blankets poofing out around him. Like a lover’s embrace, they welcomed and curled around him, lulling him deeper into the abyss of sleep– and whatever peace that perfume had granted him. 

If Phainon had wandered by his chambers, Mydei was none the wiser– nor did he care. When sleep captured him, it held him in a vice-tight grip, dreamless.

Dreamless except for the curl of that sickeningly sweet perfume and watery blue eyes.

——

When Mydei awoke, the first thing he noticed was how sweaty he was. His skin felt sticky all over, fabric and leftover grime clinging uncomfortably to it.

He groaned and sat up, “Ugh.”

Sluggishly, he kicked off the blankets and stumbled to the corner bath of his chambers. Nikador above, he’d never been more grateful for Okheman bath culture than right then, sinking into the bath with not a complaint nor a shiver of anxiety for once. The hot water sunk into his muscles and swiftly washed away all the sweat, dirt, grime, and worries from the day prior. With a pleased hum, Mydei splashed more water on himself and started to scrub. Good riddance. 

The bottles of bath oils clinked as he poured a generous amount on his hand and applied it everywhere he could reach. Steam filled the air and clouded up his mirror, which he cleaned up with a towel he soon slung around his waist.

…Hm.

Despite the steam of the hot bath, the air felt too cold, too intrusive on his bare, wet chest. It sent shivers down his spine– which was outrageous, all things considered, because what warrior couldn’t handle a few goosebumps on their skin? If Phainon heard but a single thought in his head right then, he’d have ammo for days.

Mydeimos was no shy Okheman maiden.

Yet, as Mydei walked towards his mirror with soft, padding feet, he adjusted his towel so that it fell down his abdomen and sheltered his chest from the cold. It felt right, almost natural. So much so that he hadn’t even noticed he’d done it until Mydei was face-to-face with it in his own reflective glass. He glanced down, then up. 

No longer was his mood giddy, shame and exasperation building heavy in his throat. A deep scowl curled on his lips and with a grunt, Mydei secured his towel around his waist once more. There, that was better– wasn’t it? His head throbbed, but he paid the subject no mind, reaching instead for the brush propped neatly against his vanity. 

Against the stiff bristles, his hair gave way. Locks softened by steam and oils parted seamlessly for the brush as it dragged down, down. With careful reverence, Mydei untangled every knot, big and small, even those stubborn ones that were most certainly the result of his training prior. And– though he’d never admit it– the glaring lack of a second bath that’d become custom in his routine. It was calming, in a sense, and soon the throb of his head became minute.

Expertly, he weaved his hair into its regular braid and draped his robes over his body. Something in his stomach lolled at the heaviness of his armor as he snapped it into place, but what warrior waltzed around defenseless? The Black Tide could launch an attack at any moment, and lest he fancied himself a deadweight, he’d punch it straight back to whatever hell it crawled out of.

Nikador, his head already ached something fierce just thinking about it. Mydei grit his teeth and secured his gauntlet.

The streets of Okhema were bright and alive that morning– civilians gave him curt nods as he passed, children played around his feet, and vendors fought for attention like gladiators in a ring. Their hands outstretched towards him, far more bold with his coin pouch than they were his person. 

“Lord Mydeimos, would you like new soaps?” one called, light and sweet. He brushed past.

“Weapons, fine weapons for even the most brutal Kremnoan warriors!”

A tan hand encapsulated a round, pinkish-red object, golden bracelets dangling loosely from the exposed wrist. “The newest pomegranate harvest arrived today, my Lord.”

For this, Mydei turned and politely nodded at the woman, one of the most popular– albeit far from overrated– fruit vendors on the Okheman market. This was no favoritism from him, but she was a kind soul who offered little judgement towards him or his people. Most gravitated to her for her Okheman specialties: grapes, dates, apples, and oranges. She knew, however, his sweet spot.

“This batch is quite juicy, if I do say so myself. Phagousa must have blessed us, no?”

He offered no comment. “How much per piece?”

“The same as always,” she assured, then gasped, “but silly me, I almost forgot! I set aside the best fruits for you– your arrival is always anticipated, you know–”

The vendor bent to the side, rummaging about the numerous boxes tucked neatly beneath her stand. As he’d said before, kind, thoughtful. Normally, he’d thank her graciously, but his lips were sealed firmly shut. No, before he knew it, Mydei was instead distracted by what was exposed when she leaned over.

It was nothing scandalous, nor something grand. Yet Mydei was enamoured by the sight regardless, his grip on the table tightening enough that he swore he heard the wood squeak in complaint.

Indeed, the movement exposed a small child clinging stubbornly to her skirts, even as they swished with her struggle. A boy barely tall enough to meet her thigh, with rosy cheeks and the most adorable pout known to grace Amphoreus. He tugged at the fabric insistently– that was, until wide, watery eyes glanced up to meet Mydei’s own. With a squeak, he hid behind his mother once more, saved by the vendor straightening herself once more. And alongside the boy, whatever high Mydei had been riding on plummeted. Like a bucket of water, the warmth that’d been spreading through his veins halted, replaced by something dreadfully cold. He stepped back.

His fingers twitched at his side. This happened a million times before; he was used to it. He knew that he was an intimidating man, took pride in it, in the gleam of his armor under the eternal sun and the snake of his tattoos across his exposed chest. This was nothing if not the Kremnoan way, and as Phainon had proclaimed, those who were worth his presence wouldn’t shy away with fear. It was never a problem then, it still wasn’t, but then why…

Why was insecurity lapping at his thoughts? Tainted, messy, and illogical they were, but they bounced around in his head anyway. Was he too scary? Mydei didn’t want to tower, refused to be aggressive or mean. Though he was blunt, wasn’t he? Too much.

He wanted… he wanted…

A child like that, with chubby cheeks and stubbornness that must be troublesome, but which no good parent would trade for the world. 

A child that, instead of hiding, would stumble to him cooing and babbling, sticky hands grasping for his attention. Mydei would pick them up, heart filled with love as they snuggled gleefully to his chest. And he would brush wispy white strands from their little forehead–

The crate of pomegranates landed in front of him with a dull thump. She smiled at him, her hands splayed on either side, the sleeves of her chiton flowing gracefully down strong, yet pretty, arms. Looking at it all, the insecurity turned into pure, ugly envy.

“Take your pick, Lord Mydeimos!”

He swallowed down the bitter taste on his tongue. “Of course; thank you.”

An honorable Kremnoan would never flee… But what Mydei did next was a near thing. He picked up a few pomegranates, his eyes glancing over the polished surface when his mind was registering anything but, nodded like he’d come to a grandiose decision, paid, and walked calmly– briskly– away. 

His head pounded, violent and nasty. Pain cut into his brain with every step. Kephale’s sun was too bright, the chatter of the market too loud, and damn politics, because Mydei just wanted to bury his head in the sand and never leave. What was he thinking; what was he doing?

Perhaps in the next life, his wishes could come true. But Mydei had a duty, a purpose he stood by with iron determination and would not stray from until the Era Nova was complete. This body of his was meant for bloodshed, not domesticity. The mere idea of anything otherwise was laughable.

He stormed through the streets of Okhema, chest heaving, as if the fresh air would soothe his troubles. The lighthearted conversation of citizens turned quiet and murmured, eyes upon eyes piled high on his shoulders. They mattered little.

One vendor appeared, a meek-looking thing, yet she was bold– or stupid– enough to step in his path. A large shadow fell upon her face as she held up a basket almost as large as herself for his inspection. Mydei towered, fists clenched, shaking, his mind a hazy mess, but with the final vestiges of his self-control, he gritted out, “Yes?”

“Jewelry, my Lord!” Cat ears flicked atop her head. “I couldn’t help but notice your own! Would you like…”

Her voice turned into muffled, senseless babbles. His temples burned, he could hear the pounding of his heart in his ears, and no amount of calm breaths helped him from losing his temper. Despite himself, Mydei glanced down at the contents of the basket. She spoke the truth– inside the basket was jewelry, lots of it, ranging from gold, silver, and bronze– and indeed, Mydei felt the jostle of his own necklace weigh heavy on his senses. Besides, that was warrior’s gold, and this… this was dainty, thin, and lighter on the person. He glanced up at the vendor’s feline features again; perhaps it was fashioned that way for a reason.

Nonetheless, he had no need for such frivolous purchases. Phainon already spent most of his paycheck on fake artifacts– it was only a matter of time before the man showed up at his door, wilting and holding up an empty wallet. Mydei swallowed the lump in his throat and stepped back from the vendor.

“No, thank you.” His voice sounded too deep, too rough, and too wrong to his own ears. 

She pouted, accentuating the youthful puff of her cheeks, “Are you sure? I’ll give you a discount!”

“Yes.” Mydei blinked hard and stumbled another step back. However, the hustle of the market pushed him forward again, unforgiving of his clumsiness. “I need… I need to–”

Another sharp pain stabbed his temple; his vision was still fuzzy. The voices around him were mere echoes, and he could feel his immortal body panicking, searching for a wound to mend when there was none. There was nothing. Above him, the sun felt searing, as if intending to burn away his very bones. He could’ve gasped, groaned, hissed– he wouldn’t know. All Mydei could focus on was the pain that seemed uncaring of the steel will he’d crafted after years, decades, of battle. But damn it all, he knew he didn’t cry.

The world swayed whenever he opened his eyes and made little sense when he closed them. Minutes felt like hours, and the only relief was when the world finally, blissfully, went black. If Mydei had it in him, he would’ve been grateful.

…

If was a strong word. Because if so, what was the point of passing out if he was going to awaken a few hours later? And, even though his mind had drifted and the pain had vanished, Mydei felt the rest aspect was glaringly absent. 

He wasn’t quite sure what he expected once he opened his eyes, though. Perhaps the cold gravel of the marketplace digging into his back, left out there, either too heavy or too unimportant to drag somewhere safer. Or maybe Hyacine’s clinic, now that she was briefly back in town. But his nose didn’t sting of antiseptic so… his chambers? Mydei would accept that.

But not this.

For one, Mydei was upright. Not propped-in-a-bed upright, but on his feet. The chill of the floor soaked easily into his heels.

Secondly, his coin purse was significantly lighter where it rested on his hip– he was surprised it was still there regardless. He almost chuckled to himself out of pure bewilderment. That girl certainly had the bravado of a Kremnoan, but what a pity her honor was. Yet, as his vision finally cleared completely, his heart almost stuttered to a stop.

He was in his chambers, no doubt about it.

However, laid on his vanity like a grand feast was a plethora of items Mydei did not– would never– buy. His gaze was drawn to a pinkish-red lipstick, the cap resting neatly beside it. It appeared sharp and shapely, as good as new, but a glance closer revealed the otherwise perfect surface was a little smeared. There were bigger boxes that took up most of the vanity, but they were empty. More makeup littered the space, all opened and all new.

When Mydei reached forward to grasp the lipstick, he almost dropped it. Nikador, in all their magnificent glory… There, in his reflection, someone unrecognizable stared back at him, just as wide-eyed.

They were a man, albeit it was hard to tell. Lipstick stained their mouth, bold and bright, but the corners were sharp, purposeful. High on their cheekbones, blush sat, subdued enough that one could easily reason it off as the heat of the evening. Eyeshadow, even some light eyeliner, that only served to guide Mydei’s eyes up, up to where their hair was tied gracefully.

When he gently touched the surface of the mirror, they– he– did too. Cool to the touch, soothing against the heat pooling in his veins, yet the movement caused his sleeve to droop down his forearm. But it was not his typical chiton, no, for it was devoid of tough fabrics made for battle and crimson-black patterns. That was, if what Mydei was wearing could be considered a chiton in the first place.

It was a plush pink, though that was far from his issue with it. In fact, he thought he looked rather fetching in the color, a pleased, giddy feeling spreading in his chest. Aglaea would certainly tut in approval at how it matched his makeup perfectly. But otherwise… well, it would’ve made the Council of Elders collapse from aneurysms.

The chiton had long, flowing sleeves and a skirt to match, swishing delightfully until his calves. Mydei recalled the fruit vendor, and yet his envy was all but gone now, replaced by a deep-seated satisfaction that he hadn’t experienced in quite a while– and perhaps he never had. However, as beautiful and… befitting of an Okheman woman as it was, it was painfully thin. His tattoos peeked out from beneath the fabric, curling around his muscles and sneaking underneath a lace-lined bra. Mydei shuddered. That, too, was pink. So were the matching panties.

His nails dug into the vanity table and he shook his head. This was madness. He should take it off, needed to take it off, lest it ignited a flame in him that even he couldn’t contain– but when Mydei touched the hem of his robes, he hesitated. And curse it all, his hands shook.

A knock on the door interrupted his dilemma right as Mydei thought he had enough courage to tear the damn thing off. Three knocks, light, playful, but insistent, a pattern that only belonged to one person. After a long moment of silence, the knocks echoed once more, firmer this time. 

Shit, he loathed the idea of anyone seeing him like this, but especially him. He only ever made the issue worse, and regardless, he’d never hear the end of it until he himself impossibly perished. Mydei held his breath and prayed. Perhaps if he feigned absence, that stubborn man would eventually grow bored and leave– but something deep in his chest positively purred at the idea of being seen in such a state. His fingers twitched in the direction of the doorknob.

But then, the knocks suddenly ceased. Heavy footsteps faded down the hall; Mydei released a breath he hadn’t known he’d been holding. Titans above. His shoulders slumped, his eyes fluttered shut, and he allowed his hand to rest on his vanity.

“Mydeimos!” A mop of white hair poked through his window, the only warning he got before a grown man came tumbling over his balcony.

“Phainon,” he huffed and, briefly, wondered if this was all a fever dream from a nasty hit on the head, “what–”

The man in question leapt to his feet. “You weren’t answering the door. And I thought, was the mighty Mydeimos hiding? I simply had to see for myself!”

He hadn’t faced Mydei just yet, too busy dusting off his clothes. Yet, Phainon continued to ramble.

“...I haven’t seen you much lately, you know? With all the rumors circulating lately, I became quite curious. Can you blame me, without you there to entertain me with spars?”

Phainon’s fingers visibly fumbled with the top button of his coat and there was an oddly high lilt to the end of his sentences. Mydei’s feet moved on their own, drifting closer awkwardly. Yet, his words struck a chord within him. 

“Phainon,” he repeated, this time sharper, “what are you rambling about now? Speak plainly.”

The fidgeting stopped. “Haven’t you heard? It’s silly, really. The streets were rather lively with gossip about you today. That you’ve found a lov–”

It’s only then that Phainon glanced his way, his rambles cut short by the sight that awaited him. Almost immediately, his wilted posture straightened. “Oh!”

“I have no care for what others think.” 

But instead of coming out gruff and sharp, his voice had a softer edge to it, breathy and vulnerable. Mydei’s cheeks burned fiercely. Though Phainon, on the other hand, made no effort to hide how his eyes trailed down to linger on his chest. Plumped by the bra, he had no way to cover it.

“So, when the entirety of the market saw you purchasing feminine wear without shame today, it was for… you?” For once, Phainon’s expression was unreadable.

“Yes,” he blurted without his own permission, “does it matter?”

Phainon dodged the question easily, and his glower was intense enough to make any lesser man yield. “Is this why you’ve been avoiding me? Really?”

Where days ago, Mydei’s pride might have reared its mighty head at the other’s audacity, there was nothing but an eager urge to please. Admitting the reason for his cowardice was already difficult enough, but in truth, the cross-dressing was only the tip of the iceberg– besides, there was nothing wrong with being feminine as a man. Mydei was not a prude, yet, the problem ran much deeper than something as inconsequential as a dress. His stubbornness pushed him away from Phainon.

He played with the hem of his sleeve. “Not quite.”

“‘Not quite,’ he says. Mydei, you were obviously upset by something and then suddenly, for a week, I couldn't find you anywhere. I think I deserve to know.”

Painfully, he knew Phainon spoke the truth. It was all too easy to recall days prior, when his… issue had gotten too great and he’d realized, after snapping at Phainon for something so normal– and secretly cherished– as being touchy with him, that he was only hurtful by sticking around. The great Deliverer wasted so much time on Mydei ever since they’d gotten closer, despite the judgemental whispers of Okhemans, ever the gentleman and equally a pain in the ass. He held doors open for Mydei as easily as he held his own in a fight, dragged him to the baths to cleanse him of the corruption of battle and massaged the knots from his shoulders, and never failed to defend Mydei’s honor. Sometimes, it was as simple as a friendly touch on the arm. His thighs pressed together at the memory.

It was too effortless, falling into Phainon’s arms. It fed something weak in Mydei, a part of him that would barely hesitate in rolling over and presenting his stomach. That was why it had to stop; however, Mydei had become feeble.

“Don’t blame yourself unnecessarily. It’s a personal issue.”

“You know I can’t stand seeing you like this, but I can’t help you if you’re running.” The final word was bitter, biting, and Mydei almost flinched at the sudden proximity. Phainon’s voice rumbled in his ear, a firm hand on his bicep– not aggressive, but the grip was tight enough to be a clear warning.
